title: Bloom filter
sources: Wikipedia, 'Bloom filter' (conceived by Burton Howard Bloom in 1970; bit array plus hash functions; false positive matches are possible, false negatives are not; removing an element from the simple filter is impossible; about 9.6 bits per element for a 1% error rate with optimal k) - secondary source

Example numbers: a billion usernames x about 9.6 bits = about 9.6 billion bits = about 1.2 GB (my arithmetic from the Wikipedia figure; decimal gigabytes). The 16-bit row, the hash positions and the names on screen are made-up illustrations. 'Cheap gatekeeper, never the source of truth' is a rule of thumb, not a sourced claim.

lines.text: Is this username taken? Does every one of a billion checks really need a trip to the database?
lines.caps: IS THIS *USERNAME TAKEN? | A *BILLION CHECKS | A TRIP TO THE *DATABASE?

lines.text: A Bloom filter is just a long row of bits, all starting at zero.
lines.caps: A ROW OF *BITS | ALL START AT *ZERO

lines.text: To add a name, you hash it a few times, and flip those bits to one.
lines.caps: *HASH THE NAME | FLIP THOSE BITS TO *ONE

lines.text: To check a name, you hash it the same way, and look at those bits.
lines.caps: HASH IT THE *SAME WAY | LOOK AT THOSE *BITS

lines.text: If any of them is still zero, the name is definitely free, and the database never hears about it.
If they're all ones, the name is probably taken, so only then do you ask the database.
But here's the catch: other names can flip the same bits, so you get false positives, though never false negatives, and you can't delete a name.
lines.caps: BUT THERE IS A *CATCH | FALSE *POSITIVES | NEVER FALSE *NEGATIVES | NO *DELETES

lines.text: You choose the size: about ten bits per name gives roughly one percent false positives, so a billion names fit in about one point two gigabytes.
lines.caps: ABOUT *TEN BITS PER NAME | ONE PERCENT *FALSE POSITIVES | A BILLION IN *1.2 GB

lines.text: So use it as a cheap gatekeeper in front of the database, but never as the source of truth.
lines.caps: A CHEAP *GATEKEEPER | NEVER THE *SOURCE OF TRUTH
